messages.subject: Re: using labels from column content
parts:
I don't quite understand why you want to read axislabel, but let's try a couple of things and see if something works for you.

The following is the output of my.table in dput form; this is the preferred way to send data to a text-based, R-oriented mailing list. (If it's large, save the dput output to a file, put it up on the web and post a link to it.)

# dput(my.table)       # output is copy/pasted below
my.table <- structure(list(xcol = c(1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 3L), ycol = c(234L, 
322L, 654L, 456L, 744L, 432L, 120L, 432L), axislabel = c("Region", 
"Region", "Region", "Region", "Region", "Region", "Region", "Region"
), axislab = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 3L), .Label = c("Region 1", 
"Region 2", "Region 3"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("xcol", 
"ycol", "axislabel", "axislab"), row.names = c(NA, -8L), class = "data.frame")

library(ggplot2)

# Attempt 1:
# Create a factor variable from xcol with labels Region 1 - Region 3. 
my.table$axislab <- factor(my.table$xcol, labels = paste0("Region ", 1:3))

# Remove the x-axis label
ggplot(my.table, aes(x = axislab, y = ycol)) +
    geom_boxplot() + labs(x = NULL)

# Attempt 2:
# Use scale_x_discrete() to relabel the factor levels
my.table$axislab2 <- factor(my.table$xcol, labels = rep("Region", 3))

ggplot(my.table, aes(x = axislab2, y = ycol)) +
    geom_boxplot() + labs(x = NULL) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = rep("Region", 3))

# Attempt 3:
# Get rid of the tick marks and axis text, just leave the axis title
# The argument of labs is a bad hack, though - in this case, a manual
# specification is less messy.

ggplot(my.table, aes(x = factor(xcol), y = ycol)) +
   geom_boxplot() +
   theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
         axis.ticks.x = element_blank()) +
   labs(x = unique(DF$axislabel)[1])

Hope one of these is close to what you were after.

Dennis
